doc.title: Buddy Collette interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: Famous students: Eric Dolphy, James Newton and others
summary: Rowe notes musicians' reverence for Collette; he names students including Dolphy, Newton, Sonny Criss.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Do you know that you’re one of those fellows that when you talk to other musicians, they have great reverence for you.

Well that’s very nice to hear that, thank you, yeah. I do have a lot of friends and I’ve done a lot of teaching and of course a lot of those, some of them I had the pleasure of working with, are great players out there today, so I’m so happy to hear them. They send their love and they come to say hello and they call. You know it’s a really great feeling.
As long as we’re on that subject, why don’t you just drop a few names to me, because I know you have taught —

Well one of the greats of course, Eric Dolphy, I taught him many years, probably 1949, ’50. And hence he went on to go with the Chico Hamilton band, not right after I left, but I think Paul Horn, I didn’t teach Paul but he was a good friend of mine, we have a lot in common, and after I think Paul left I think Eric went in the band after Paul. So a couple of others are James Newton, the flutist, and Big Jim McNeely, Sonny Criss, let’s see the other names, John Stevens, I don’t know if you know him, he’s a fine musician here in L.A.
Well that’s quite an amazing list. © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
